## 9. Full resource statement and first-stage composition

Let C_D be the actual cost of the supplied system block encodings and their controlled selection, plus the explicit linear oscillator block. Let q=polylog[S(A0+1)/epsilon] be the inner Dyson order, and B=polylog[M,K,R,v,T,1/epsilon] the finite time/arithmetic precision. An explicit, deliberately nonoptimized gate upper bound has the form

    O(S A0 {q[O~(M^2 K)+C_D]+poly(M,r,B,input bits)}),

with polynomially many workspace bits in M,r,log(K),q,B and the actual system input size. Every Gaussian gate, jump direction, CDF prefix, phase, source list and amplification call is acquired above. R appears only through B and the supplied input bits. The dependence on T can be high: with the coarse vacuum cutoff K=O((aT)^2+log(1/epsilon)), the bound is not a near-linear-T theorem and does not establish a practical crossover.

For the actual stage-one bath, M=O(log^2(T/epsilon)), ||c||^2 is bounded, and its one-particle R grows only polynomially with T/epsilon while its parameter synthesis uses polynomial logarithmic guard bits. Receive its spectrum-to-channel bound, select K from its proved factorial tail, and allocate separate epsilon budgets to spectrum error, Fock cutoff, parameter rounding, actual count cap, source arithmetic, clocks and digital synthesis. With the stated precision-cost condition on the supplied system access, all terms above then have POLYLOGARITHMIC inverse-accuracy dependence at fixed T,h,a. This is a candidate complete-operation consequence beyond a mode-count statement. It does not assume the hierarchy is an exact thermal reservoir, and the first-stage two-quantum obstruction remains intact.

The detailed finite arithmetic, binary Fock gate construction, tiny-prefix bound, robust amplification argument and emitted-count factorial proof are supplied in FINITE_BIT_DETAILS.md. The matched complete-pipeline comparison is in PRIOR_COMPARISON.md. The derivation still requires an independent review of the whole finite-bit conjunction and a historical-priority assessment. No universal superiority over every reparameterization or physical platform follows from this theorem.

## Composing the actual operation

Each complete first-event circuit has a local isometry error that includes clock embedding, source arithmetic, Dyson tail, Gaussian gates and amplification leakage. Its induced channel error is at most twice that error. Compare the implemented capped process backwards against exact first-event instruments; CPTP continuation cannot enlarge a preceding error. This yields at most `S` local costs. The exact count-tail bound, charged tiny remaining windows, and actual prescribed system instruments complete the comparison. Rounding a private event time changes the exact continuation by at most `O(v+KR)` times the time error. Hence resolving it requires logarithmically many additional time bits.

Round `H` Hermitian and keep the loss supplied as a rounded factor `E`, forming the damping matrix from that factor. Then CP is preserved. On the finite cutoff, coefficient perturbations in the generator have norm bounded by a polynomial in `K,||E||,h,q_j` times their absolute entry errors. Contractive Duhamel multiplies this by `T`, so the precision requirement is logarithmic in `R,T,1/epsilon`, not a separate rate-dependent number of gates. The spectrum and infinite-Fock errors are received separately from the frozen first-stage derivation.

These details support a constructive polynomial upper bound. They do not supply an optimized fault-tolerant circuit, independent proof review or a practical runtime advantage.

# Response-exact positive rational baths: construction and boundaries

Status: independently derived candidate primitive, not audited externally, no novelty/advantage claim. Single-worker derivation. Source/cost comparison is in REPORT.md. Units hbar=omega_c=1, and Fourier convention C(t)=(2pi)^-1 int S(w) exp(-iwt)dw.

## Consequential operation and actual target

A bounded Hermitian system coupling operator Q, arbitrary finite-dimensional controlled H_S(t), factorized initial system/bath state, zero-mean stationary Gaussian continuum. We seek the complete reduced channel on every input (including a reference) up to T. No RWA, weak-coupling limit or spectral gap is assumed. The model proved here is the zero-temperature Ohmic continuum

    S_*(w) = alpha (|w|+w)/(1+w^2)^2, alpha>0.

It corresponds to J(w)=alpha w/[pi(1+w^2)^2] on w>0. It is genuinely gapless; its positive-frequency spectrum has a nonanalytic edge at 0. Its imaginary correlation is exactly

    Im C_*(t)=-(alpha/4) t exp(-t), t>=0.

Its symmetrized fluctuations have a long tail. A finite rational spectrum cannot equal S_* globally; it can approximate it with a quantified excess of classical noise.

## Failure A: independently damped positive modes

For C_L(t)=sum_j v_j exp[-(gamma_j+i Omega_j)t], v_j>0, gamma_j>0, the two-sided spectrum is a positive sum of Lorentzians. At every real w it is strictly positive. In particular S_L(0)=sum_j 2v_j gamma_j/(gamma_j^2+Omega_j^2)>0. The target S_*(0)=0 and S_*(w)=0 for w<0. In a commuting dephasing experiment, the integrated real influence has asymptotic slope S_L(0)/2>0, whereas the Ohmic target grows logarithmically. Positive weights cannot cancel this slope. This does not forbid a finite-horizon approximation with T-dependent parameters, nor prove a lower bound against coupled modes.

At any finite beta>0, a nonzero rational spectrum cannot satisfy S(-w)=exp(-beta w)S(w) on an open frequency interval: its rational ratio would equal a nonrational exponential by analytic continuation. Exact finite-mode global KMS is therefore the wrong target. At beta=infinity, a nonzero rational spectrum cannot vanish on a whole negative half-line. Exact balance at finitely many frequencies remains possible.
